newsitem.title: CAMEROON: U.N. team arrives to assess Nigeria-Cameroon row.
newsitem.headline: U.N. team arrives to assess Nigeria-Cameroon row.

text.p: A United Nations team has arrived in Yaounde at the start of an assessment mission into frequent border clashes between Nigeria and Cameroon in the Bakassi peninsula, Radio Cameroon said on Sunday.
The mission, led by a special representative of U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, arrived on Saturday and is scheduled to meet Cameroon President Paul Biya on Monday.
The officials will visit Bakassi, a string of impoverished islands in the oil-rich Gulf of Guinea, before flying to the Nigerian capital Abuja, the radio said.
Nigerian and Cameroonian troops have clashed over the Bakassi peninsula since February 1994 and the two countries accuse each other of massing forces in the area.
